title: Humans follow earth; the Dao follows what is naturally so
subtitle: Daodejing, chapter 25
timeLabel: Pre-Qin text · continuously commented on through the Tang
shortSummary: The line orders humans, earth, heaven, Dao and naturalness in a chain of following, opening a path into the classical meaning of ziran.
curatorialDescription: Ziran here is closer to “being so of itself” than to the modern scientific category of nature.

Tang readers encountered the Daodejing within a long commentarial history. The museum separates primary text, commentators and later institutions instead of assuming that one sentence had a single unchanged meaning.
The passage can connect with mountains, cultivation and political non-coercion, but each relation requires a specific context.
researchNote: The first release locates the line in chapter 25 of the received text. Future versions will add manuscript and major commentarial variants.

quote.original: 人法地，地法天，天法道，道法自然。
quote.interpretation: Human order follows earth, earth follows heaven, and heaven follows the Dao; the Dao unfolds not by an external command but in a way that is so of itself.
